name: default
description: The default tagging vocabulary for Bookmark Sorter piles: four dimensions, ordinary tags with no prefix.
notes: A dimension is one axis of description. An item may take tags from every dimension, and any number of tags within a dimension.
Tags are deliberately overlapping: california and usa on the same item is correct, not a mistake.
Tag names are stored exactly as written here. Bookmark Sorter selection keys lowercase them and turn punctuation into dashes, so business_economics is selected as business-economics.

dimensions.name: topic
notes: Assign every topic that applies. One to three is usual; more is fine when the item genuinely spans them.
Assign the narrower topic and the broader one together when both apply: an item on model training takes ai and technology; an item on emissions policy takes climate, environment, and politics.

tag_notes.media: Journalism, publishing, broadcasting, and platforms as a subject, not the fact that the item is itself a news story.
tag_notes.covid_19: The pandemic and its aftermath specifically. Ordinary public health goes to health.
tag_notes.ai: Machine learning and its products, research, and consequences. Also assign technology.
tag_notes.social_justice: Race, gender, inequality, migration, disability, and civil rights as a subject.

dimensions.name: location
dimensions.description: The places the item is about.
notes: This is the subject's location, not the publisher's. A New York Times report on Lagos is africa, not usa.
Assign the specific place and the broader places that contain it. The containment tags this vocabulary knows about are added for you.
Assign nothing when an item has no particular place.

tag_notes.developing_countries: A judgement about the item's framing, not a fixed list of states. Assign it when the item is about development, aid, or low- and middle-income economies as such.

dimensions.name: period
dimensions.description: The period the item's content belongs to.
notes: Use the era the item is about when it is historical, and its publication date otherwise.
Evidence, in order: a date in the title or note, a date in the URL, then the item's added date.
Assign nothing when neither the subject period nor the date can be established. A guess here is worse than a gap.

tag_notes.pre-2000: Everything up to and including the year 2000.

dimensions.name: sourcetype
notes: Judge from the host name first, then the title. Usually exactly one tag.
Assign nothing rather than guessing when the host says nothing useful.

tag_notes.major_publication: An established newspaper, magazine, broadcaster, wire service, or academic journal.
tag_notes.blogger: A personal site, newsletter, or writing platform account: Substack, Medium, a named individual's domain.
tag_notes.corporation: A company's own site: product pages, documentation, engineering and corporate blogs.
tag_notes.ngo: A non-profit, foundation, advocacy group, research institute, or university that is not run by a government.
tag_notes.government: A government agency or intergovernmental body, including .gov and .gov.* hosts and bodies such as the UN and the WHO.
